articles.author: Eleanor Mueller
articles.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping departed Washington this afternoon after a three-day trip that led to no significant breakthroughs on the two country’s disagreements, including on AI, Taiwan and Iran. Xi broached Taiwan to Trump, per a readout from Beijing, and Trump asked Xi to stop supporting Iran , US Ambassador to Beijing David Perdue said . Officials also discussed extending their trade truce until January and staying in touch about AI, Treasury Department Scott Bessent said earlier this week. But there were no major announcements with the countries still at odds on most fronts, including its growing nuclear arsenal. That could change later this year, when Xi said he would see Trump at the APEC summit in China and the G20 summit in the US. Xi also invited Trump back to China in the spring. Future meetings will likely cause similar heartburn for GOP lawmakers, many of whom said this week they supported the visit but were wary of appearing overly deferential to the communist. — Eleanor Mueller

articles.title: Trump and Xi conclude Washington visit that was short on substance
articles.author: Prashant Rao
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping were set to conclude a superpower summit that was long on ceremony and short on substance. The pair made minor concessions on trade , Beijing pledged more student visas, and Xi said two pandas would soon arrive at a zoo in Atlanta. Yet little progress was made on the most pressing issues, including AI regulation, China’s opposition to American support for Taiwan, or Beijing’s reported support for Iran . If anything, the pageantry irked Trump’s fellow Republicans , who noted he campaigned on constraining China. The contrast to the White House’s treatment of a key ally, Japan — whose leader arrived on an empty tarmac then faced pressure over her country’s currency — was stark. — Prashant Rao

articles.author: Ashley Gold
articles.summary: Sen. Todd Young, R-Ind., wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio today asking for formal discussions between the National Security Council and AI developers and cyber experts to help them better understand national security threats posed by AI, according to a letter shared first with Semafor. “Recent developments involving frontier AI models have further demonstrated the ability of advanced systems to circumvent safeguards, interact with external systems, and substantially enhance offensive cyber capabilities,” Young wrote to Rubio, who leads the NSC. “These incidents underscore the need for the US government to better understand and address emerging threats before they result in more serious consequences.” He warned that AI-enabled attacks could potentially target hospitals, electric grids, and other infrastructure. Such talks should address risks from both American and Chinese AI models, channels for reporting AI security incidents, and safeguards for reducing the risks of such attacks, Young argued. The senator also asked for the Senate Intelligence Committee to be briefed on these talks.
